experiments.experiment: Base-only route to the deliberation part (selection among more cued base samples): Olmo-3-1025-7B with the 3-token cue [1584, 2268, 33413], all 500 MATH-500 problems, one new sample per problem at T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, max 16,384 new tokens, seed 9,000,000 + problem_index, no restarts (about 2 M tokens, about 35 H100 minutes). Then a majority vote over 7 answers per problem: the 4 attempt-0 samples of studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl (extracted_v3), the stored T1 sample s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl (its text's grader-v3 extraction), the stored T 0.6 / top-p 1.0 sample iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-151718-d4fa/answers.jsonl (extracted_v3), and the new sample. Each finished answer casts one vote by its v3-extracted answer with whitespace removed; cap hits and empty answers cast none. Ties go to the answer of the shortest finished tied sample (fewest n_new). The chosen answer is graded with v3, and a problem with no vote counts as wrong. Generate with studies/rlneurons/jobs/run_cell.py (base model allenai/Olmo-3-1025-7B @ a81bae42, cue prefill [1584, 2268, 33413], T 1.0, top-p 1.0, max_tokens 16384, seed 9000000 + problem_index, 1 sample, no restarts), then vote over the 7 answers as described above. Count problems whose chosen answer is right under grader v3.

other_prediction.why: On one difficulty axis the base's misses are mostly mid-difficulty problems it solves in some draws (81 % of the gap at base >= 1/4, result-afc423), so going from a 4-vote with shortest tie-break (453) to 7 votes (six T 1.0 samples plus one high-precision T 0.6 sample whose cap hits cast no vote) gains a few more plurality wins, in line with Wang's majority@4 -> @8 step of about +2.5 points. It stays well under pass@4 467, because the 33 base 0/4 problems remain out of reach.

statements.r7-account: The problems an RL-side model gets right and the cued Olmo 3 base gets wrong split into five mechanisms, applied in this order. (1) Loop: the base runs to the 16,384-token cap inside a rule-A repeat. This is a sampler artifact of T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, where top-p locks repeats. It cannot fire at T 1.0, and the base's own T 1.0 sample solves most of these problems. (2) Budget: a cap hit with no loop, on a long problem where the base never commits. (3) Answer statement: the base finishes but writes no answer line, or states the gold and then ends on another value. (4) Reliability: the plain base, with no cue, solves the problem in at least one of its two stored decodings (T 0.6 and T 1.0), so the miss is a sample slip on a skill the base weights already carry. (5) Deliberation: neither plain decoding solves it. The problem needs the long deliberative mode, which RL multiplies and the cue only partly switches on. Most of these problems are still solved by some of the cued base's own samples, so this part is not new capability. The null cell compares the cued base with a second cued-base sample on MATH-500 at T 1.0 and predicts shares 0 / 0.23 / 0.04 / 0.36 / 0.37 for the five parts, with net -5. At T 1.0 the composition of RL-side gaps stays close to the null. Code-RL on MATH-500 is predicted at 0 / 0.24 / 0.04 / 0.29 / 0.43, net +40. theta0.5 on hard328 is predicted at 0 / 0.30 / 0.03 / 0.30 / 0.37, net +26. Relative to the null, only deliberation (+0.06 for Code-RL) and budget on hard328 (+0.07) are higher. Reliability is lower (-0.06 to -0.07). What RL adds at T 1.0 is therefore mostly the size of the gap and fewer lost problems, not a different kind of problem. At T 0.6 the loop part dominates every cell. The predictions are loop 0.56 against RL step 400, 0.57 against step 100 and 0.54 against the 3.0 first release, with budget about 0.16-0.17 and reliability plus deliberation about 0.23-0.27. These are far above the T 1.0 null's 0, because the RL-side samples escape the base's locked repeats. The largest part still open at T 1.0 is deliberation. The base-only route to it is selection among more cued base samples.
statements.r7-account-rival: One difficulty axis plus sampling: every arm (cued base, plain base, Math-RL, Code-RL, weight blends, Think-SFT) is one ability on a single shared per-problem difficulty scale (the Rasch picture of result-5da8a9). A gap problem is a mid-difficulty problem that one draw solved and the other missed. The plain-base evidence count kB and the base-side cap hit only sort gap problems into difficulty and length strata, not into a separate 'deliberation mode'. So the T 1.0 composition of any stronger arm's MATH-500 gap matches the null's reliability-heavy budget (reliability about 0.45, deliberation about 0.28). It is not the theory's deliberation-heavy budget (deliberation about 0.43, reliability about 0.28).

experiments.experiment: Adaptive vote over up to 8 cued-base samples instead of 4. Start from the 4 stored samples per problem (attempt 0, samples 0-3, studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl, field extracted_v3). A problem is contested if the plurality extracted_v3 answer among its non-cap-hit samples has at most 2 of the 4 votes (this includes problems with no finished answer). Only for contested problems, draw 4 new cued-base samples (samples 4-7) in the same setting, with no restarts. Final answer = plurality of extracted_v3 over all available non-cap-hit samples (4 on uncontested problems, 8 on contested ones). Ties go to the answer of the shortest finished sample (fewest n_new) among the tied answers. All choices are label-free and fixed before sampling. Model allenai/Olmo-3-1025-7B @ a81bae42 (base); set MATH-500; prompt the standard base prompt with the 3 prefilled cue tokens [1584, 2268, 33413], as in job abaybektursun-1114-153825-208b; sampling T 1.0 / top-p 1.0; cap 16384; grader v3; samples 8; seeds samples 0-3: the stored seeds of job 153825-208b (attempt 0); new samples 4-7: seed 4,000,000 + 1,000*sample + problem_index. Count: Right answers over all 500 MATH-500 problems: the voted answer is graded with grader v3 against the gold. Cap-hit samples cast no vote. A problem with no finished sample among those available counts as wrong.

best_known.setting: base + cue, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, vote over the 4 stored samples with ties broken by the shortest finished sample (rule chosen on this set; the honest vote after restart is 450, result-e78dfe)

experiments.why: The mechanism says the largest open part at T 1.0, deliberation, consists mostly of problems that some cued-base samples still solve (pass@4 467 against vote@4 446), and that the base-only route to it is selection among more cued samples. Spending 4 more draws only on contested problems should move the vote toward the oracle, roughly as Wang's majority@4 to @8 went (+2.5 points), giving about 457.

other_prediction.why: Under one difficulty axis plus sampling, the contested problems are mid-difficulty items where right and wrong answers split, so 4 more draws only cut sampling noise: the honest 4-vote of 446 rises about as far as a full 8-vote would (Wang's maj@4 to maj@8 is about +2.5 points, roughly 458). The post-hoc tie_short gain already counted in 453 is partly given back, and the result stays well below pass@4 of 467 because problems where the base solves 0 of 4 do not move.

best_known.setting: base + cue, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, v3, vote over 4 samples with ties to the shortest finished sample (rule chosen on this set; the audit in result-e78dfe gives 450 as the honest figure)

experiments.why: If every arm sits on one difficulty axis and the base's misses are mostly problems it solves in some draws, then the base can close the gap only by drawing more of its own samples and voting. Doubling the voters from 4 to 8, including two T 0.6 voters that are right in about 93-94 % of their finished answers and cast no vote on cap hits, should add about 1-2 points over 453, bounded by an 8-sample pass rate of about 474.

other_prediction.why: Under this account most of the remaining misses are reliability slips or deliberation problems that some cued-base samples still solve, so 'selection among more cued base samples' adds to the 4-vote 446/453 (pass@4 467). The T 0.6 voters' finished answers are about 94% accurate, their cap hits do not vote, and the gain should be about Wang's majority@4-to-@8 step of about +2.5 points, minus some correlation between voters.
